commitResults.messageBody:
The sort command hides past visits and replaces the active filter.
This makes past schedules unavailable for reference and prevents users
from sorting a focused list of patients.

later before past visits, and order each group by date and time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require date field for sort command
commitResults.messageBody:
The sort command accepts missing or unrelated arguments because the
parser ignores its input. This makes the command difficult to extend
with additional sort fields.

Route sort arguments through a dedicated parser. Accept only `date`,
and show the standard usage message for missing, unsupported, or
additional arguments.

Update parser tests and guides to use `sort date`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refine current and future user stories

commitResults.messageBody: Branch refine user stories
Route requested input through Logic without command parsing and let command results control when the address book is saved. Allow blank responses while a request is pending.
Prompt before delete and clear mutations, consume every non-y response as cancellation, and avoid unnecessary saves. Cover confirmation, cancellation, stale targets, and empty input flows.
Describe the delete and clear confirmation workflows, reusable follow-up input mechanism, persistence behavior, diagrams, and manual test cases.
Align the guides with the existing save policy while documenting the new no-write prompt and cancellation results.
Confirm the pending delete request before asserting the displayed and stored person lists after sorting.
Add delete/clear confirmation
Store session commands with a movable history position and preserve unfinished input as a draft. Exclude follow-up responses so confirmation input does not pollute command history.

Record each normal command submission before execution and connect Up and Down arrow events to history navigation. Keep follow-up responses out of history so confirmation input remains separate from commands.
Explain the user workflow, UI design, session lifetime, and manual checks for command history. Update the UI diagram and align the sorting test with delete confirmation.

Skip exact consecutive duplicates so arrow navigation always produces a visible change when an older command exists. Preserve duplicates that are separated by another command and reset navigation after every submission.
Clarify that consecutive exact duplicates share one history entry while duplicates separated by another command remain available. Add manual checks for both cases.

Exercise the production FXML handlers for command submission and history navigation, including success, failure, follow-up input, caret placement, and event consumption. Run Linux CI inside a virtual display so the JavaFX tests remain portable.
